Figure caption: Schematic illustration of optimizing and screening of LNPsTwenty-five types of LNPs are formulated with variations in lipid types and percentages (for details see Figure 2). After in vitro characterization and expression analysis in multiple cell lines, the LNP library is prepared by co-encapsulating mRNA and LNP-specific DNA barcodes. The libraries are then injected i.v. into mice, and the biodistribution of the LNPs is assessed by deep sequencing of samples derived from the extracted tissues. Finally, a validation study is conducted by applying the individual LNP candidates to mice

Figure caption: Composition and characterization of the LNPs(A) Composition of the LNPs (weight percentages of total). (B) Influence of helper lipid (DOPE and DOPC) weight percentages on LNP size. (C) Influence of C14120 weight percentages on the size of TPGS- and DSPE-PEG-containing LNPs. (D) Influence of PEG-lipid (TPGS and DSPE-PEG) weight percentages on LNP size. (E) Change in LNP size upon mRNA loading as a function of TPGS weight percentage (N/P ratio = 12). Data show mean ± SD (n = 3). Pearson correlation coefficients were used for correlation analysis, and the corresponding p values and R2 values are displayed on each plot.

Figure caption: Cell type and origin dependency of in vitro mCherry expression for individual LNPs measured 24 h post-transfection(A) Histograms showing mCherry expression in bEnd3 (blue) and AML12 (red) cells upon transfection with LNPs formulated with different types of PEG-lipids (TPGS and DSPE-PEG) in comparison to respective untransfected sample (Ctrl). (B and C) mCherry expression levels, with regard to data shown in (A) but including a Lipofectamine 2000 (LIPO) transfection control. (D) mCherry expression level as a function of PEG-lipid percentages (DSPE-PEG and TPGS) in ARPE-19, Hep G2, AML12, and HEK293-H. Data are presented as mean ± SD (n = 3); ∗∗p < 0.01, ∗∗∗∗p < 0.0001. Significance was determined by independent t test. Pearson correlation coefficients were used for correlation analysis, and the corresponding p values and R2 values are displayed on each plot.

Figure caption: In vivo delivery of the barcoded LNP library encapsulated with Luc-mRNA enabled the identification of specific LNPs by subsequent barcode sequencing from individual organs(A) Heatmap showing the normalized DNA counts in various organs measured at 24 h after i.v. injection of LNPs. (B) PCA of normalized DNA counts showing the separation of different tissue clusters.

Figure caption: Luciferase expression in various organs using selected organ-targeted LNP candidates and compared to Moderna formulation(A–D) (A) SM102, (B) lung-targeting LNP8 (C), liver-targeting LNP11, and (D) spleen-targeting LNP14. The IVIS image is shown in (A–D), and the average intensity of the region of interest is shown in (E). (F) The luminescence ratio of lung or spleen to each individual liver signal (F). Data are presented as mean ± SD (n = 3). ∗∗∗p < 0.001; ns, not significant. Significance was determined by independent t test. (G and H) Representative images of mCherry immunohistochemical staining in normal lung tissue sections from two individually treated mice. Positive mCherry signals, visualized by brown 3,3′-diaminobenzidine (DAB) chromogen and indicated by arrows, are localized to scattered pneumocytes along the alveolar surface. Sections were counterstained with hematoxylin to visualize nuclei. Images are shown at both overview and high magnification. Scale bars: 100 μm (overview) and 50 μm (high magnification).
